meta.title: Two Red Balls
meta.textType: story: a mix-up, with pronouns to follow

paragraphs: On Monday, November ninth, Tom took Pip to the park at four o'clock. Ben and Hugo waited for them under a big tree. Hugo was a boy in Tom's class, and he had a red football. Tom had a red football, too. The two balls looked the same. The boys sat on the bench, and Pip sat on the grass next to them. "What do you like doing?" asked Hugo.

"I like playing football," said Tom. "I want to be a football player." "I enjoy playing chess, and I am good at it," said Hugo. "I enjoy drawing," said Ben, "and I draw a lot of animals." At that moment, Pip took one of the red balls and ran across the grass. The ball was too big for him, but he ran very fast. "Stop, Pip!" shouted Tom. Tom, Ben, and Hugo jumped up, and they ran after the puppy. Pip probably thought that it was a game.

Pip dropped the ball under a tree, and Tom picked it up. "That is my ball!" said Tom. "No, it is mine!" said Hugo. The two boys looked at each other. For a moment, nobody spoke. "Whose ball is it?" asked Ben. "Is it Tom's or Hugo's?" Ben decided to look at the ball more carefully. It had a white patch with a name on it in black marker: "HUGO." "It is Hugo's," said Ben. "Are you sure?" asked Tom. "Yes, I am sure," said Ben, and he showed him the name. Tom gave the ball to Hugo. Then Pip ran back and fetched the other ball. He brought it to Tom. Hugo gave Tom the marker. Tom wrote his own name on the white patch.

"Pip did not break anything," said Hugo, and he laughed. "He is a good dog, but he can mix up two balls." "What will happen next time?" asked Ben. "Nothing will happen," said Tom, "because now each ball has a name." Instead of going home, Tom and Hugo decided to play together. Tom wanted to be a football player, so he kicked his ball to Hugo. Hugo kicked it back. Ben took out his notebook and began to draw.

Ben drew the two red balls, the three boys, and a small brown puppy. Pip lay down on the grass between the balls. He was tired after the long run. "Whose picture is this?" asked Tom. "It is my picture, and it is for all of you," said Ben. Pip closed his eyes and probably dreamed about a third ball.
